newsitem.title: USA: Mass. supermarket magnate ordered to pay $200 million.
newsitem.headline: Mass. supermarket magnate ordered to pay $200 million.

text.p: A Massachusetts judge Tuesday ordered a supermarket magnate and his children to pay about $200 million to the family of his late brother as distributions in a stock fraud case.

Massachusetts State Superior Court Judge Maria Lopez ordered Telemachus (Mike) Demoulas and his children to pay $206 million to the widow and family of his late borther George Demoulas, according to Bozell Sawyer Miller Group, a public relations firm for the George Demoulas family lawyers.
The same court found in 1994 that Mike Demoulas defrauded Evanthea Demoulas, the widow of his late brother, and her children of assets over a 20-year period, according to the public relations agency.

The two brothers shared the Massachusetts-based Demoulas Super Markets -- which has more than 50 stores along the Massachuetts and New Hampshire coast -- until George's death in 1971. Upon George's death, the two families each owned half of the company, the public relations firm said.

"This is the amount of money that would have been due to the plaintiffs from these stocks had they not been systematically defrauded by the other side of the family over a period of 20 years," Robert Gerrard and Carol Cohen, lawyers for the George Demoulas family, said in a statement.

The judgment reaffirmed an earlier order to remove Mike Demoulas from an executive position at Demoulas Super Markets, although his family will be allowed to appoint two other family members to the company's seven-member board of directors.

Grant Gregory, a financial advisor for the George Demoulas family, said the ruling leaves Demoulas Super Markets on "strong and competitive financial footing and positions it well for significant growth in the near future."
